unruled:gate:ny_it201.mctmt_possible#1.class: no gate defect; non-Schedule C self-employment is refused federally
unruled:gate:ny_it201.mctmt_possible#1.reason: As the earlier ruling, rechecked: K-1s, farm income and clergy are still refused federally. One WIDE accepted.

findings.evidence: Outside the tool's scope, refused federally before New York is reached: partnership K-1s by scope.k1 and farm income by scope.farm (both in scope.schedule1), clergy by scope.clergy_if_religious_work (scope.schedule1), and other self-employment not on Schedule C by person.se_screened. Within the tool the only self-employment income is Schedule C, which ny_it201.mctmt_people reads (its note).

Outside the tool's scope, refused federally before New York is reached: partnership K-1s by scope.k1 and farm income by scope.farm (both in scope.schedule1), clergy by scope.clergy_if_religious_work (scope.schedule1), and other self-employment not on Schedule C by person.se_screened. Within the tool the only self-employment income is Schedule C, which ny_it201.mctmt_people reads (its note).
ny_it201i p. 15: the test is net earnings allocated to a zone; a Schedule C profit over $50,000 outside the zones asks ny_it201.ask.mctmt, which then answers No. One extra question.

unruled:gate:ny_it201.federal_care#1.class: no gate defect; the federal prompts name the spouse and the student or disabled spouse
unruled:gate:ny_it201.federal_care#1.reason: The findings read the federal questions' labels; their bank prompts and help cover both cases. One WIDE accepted.

findings.evidence: f2441.care help (interview/2025/questions.yaml): 'On a joint return, so does care that let one of you work while the other studied full time or could not care for themselves.' (BUG-0447, fixed by BUG-0682.) The prompt: 'did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) use or pay for care ... so that you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) could work or look for work?'
The f2441.care prompt names the spouse ('did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) use or pay for care') and its help says 'whoever paid'; f2441.benefits names the spouse's employer.
ny_it216i p. 1: a filer who fails another federal test reaches ny_it201.ask.dependent_care for nothing; that question then answers No. One extra question.

unruled:gate:ny_it201.has_pension_income.class: defect, medium: the gate misses a government disability pension reported as wages
unruled:gate:ny_it201.has_pension_income.reason: Disability pensions before the minimum retirement age are now computed federally on line 1h, so they never reach IT-201 lines 9 or 10. Evaluated. The public-authority UNCLEAR is answered by the follow-up question; one WIDE accepted.

findings.evidence: ny_it201i p. 9, Line 26: "Did you receive a pension or other distribution from a New York State or local government pension plan or federal government pension plan that was included in your federal adjusted gross income?". The earlier ruling (refused federally) no longer holds: retirement.dis_wages now sends a disability pension paid wholly before the minimum retirement age to Form 1040 line 1h. Evaluated (/tmp/xrel/ny/dis_inputs.json): f1040.line1h $18,000, ny_it201.line9 and line10 $0, has_pension_income false, gov_pension_if_income false, line26 $0, no refusal.
Same cause: the gate (lines 9 and 10, from the line 29 text's 'generally reported on line 9 or 10') is narrower than line 26's 'included in your federal adjusted gross income'.

After a No to ny_it201.ask.gov_pension, ny_it201.ask.gov_pension_other asks 'Was any of it from the MTA, MABSTOA, the Long Island Rail Road, or a SUNY, CUNY or State Education Department plan (such as TIAA)?' with the help 'These public plans count as government pensions in New York.' (gate ny_it201.gov_said_no). A U.S. territory or the District of Columbia is in the input's source but not in the shown prompt; noted in BUG-0850's proposed fix.
A private pension or IRA makes the gate true; the government pension questions then answer No. Extra questions only.

unruled:ny_it201.ask.dependent_care#1.reason: Line 64 screen: whether the care paid for would qualify for the federal child and dependent care credit; Yes refuses line 64 (Form IT-216), No computes $0.

findings.evidence: The gate ny_it201.federal_care is computed from f2441.care, 'did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) pay for, or incur expenses for, the care of a qualifying person so that you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) could work or look for work' (forms/2025/f2441.yaml:41-47). IT-216-I p. 1 puts the spouse in the same test ('The care was provided so you (and your spouse, if you were married) could work or look for work'), so a filer who reaches line 64 has already affirmed the spouse's payment.

ny_it201i p. 19, Line 64 asks 'Would you qualify to claim the federal child and dependent care credit', and IT-216-I p. 1 adds 'if you did not find a job and have no earned income for the year, you cannot take the credit'. A literal Yes from a filer with no earned income only refuses line 64, whose correct amount is zero.

unruled:ny_it201.ask.gov_pension#1.reason: Two WIDE accepted; the UNCLEAR on the employer list is the federal-government clause and the source's own "certain public authorities, including".

findings.evidence: ny_it201i p. 9, Line 26: periodic 457 distributions may not be subtracted, so line 26 is 0; the filer who answers Yes is refused for nothing (and ny_it201.ask.pension_exclusion names such distributions too). Safe.
ny_it201i p. 9, Line 26: private-university and supplemental-annuity parts may not be subtracted; a TIAA recipient answering Yes is refused for nothing. Safe.

ny_it201i p. 9, Line 26 lists "The United States, its territories, possessions (or political subdivisions thereof), or any agency or instrumentality of the United States (including the military)". The question's "a federal government pension plan" covers an agency or instrumentality, and "a U.S. territory" a possession or its subdivision in ordinary reading. Other public authorities: the source itself says "Certain public authorities, including" the three the question names. A wrong No leaves line 26 at 0, overstating New York tax; a filer 59 1/2 or older is still refused by ny_it201.ask.pension_exclusion ("other than a government pension subtracted on line 26").

unruled:ny_it201.ask.mctmt#1.reason: The combined-zones reading leans WIDE; the undefined Zone 2 is a low wording gap (BUG-0450).

findings.evidence: ny_it201i p. 15: the test is per zone and per person ("allocated to either zone exceed $50,000"; notes to lines 54a and 54b). Reading the question as Zone 1 plus Zone 2 combined only gives Yes and a refusal where the tool's 0 is right. Safe.

ny_it201i p. 15: "Zone 2 includes the counties of: Dutchess, Nassau, Orange, Putnam, Rockland, Suffolk, Westchester". The question says only "Zone 2" and the help "the suburban counties (Zone 2)"; a filer with earnings over $50,000 allocated to such a county may answer No, and lines 54a and 54b are 0 with the MCTMT omitted. No other question covers it. Low; BUG-0450.

unruled:ny_it201.ask.pension_exclusion#1.reason: WIDE only; each finding refuses a filer whose qualifying amount is 0.

findings.evidence: ny_it201i p. 9, Line 29: lump sums qualify only from an IRA or an HR-10 plan; a filer with only a non-qualifying lump sum is refused though line 29 is 0. Safe.
ny_it201i pp. 9-10, Line 29: QDRO distributions to a nonemployee spouse, annuities bought with own funds and post-retirement contributions do not qualify; such filers are refused for nothing. Safe.
ny_it201i p. 9, Line 29: "If you became 59 1/2 during 2025, enter only the amount you received after you became 59 1/2"; income received entirely before is refused for nothing. Safe.

unruled:ny_it201.ask.refund_529#1.reason: Real, low gap: "part of a refund" may draw No from a filer wanting the whole refund deposited (BUG-0449).

findings.evidence: ny_it201i p. 23, Line 78a: "You may directly deposit all or a portion of your refund". The question and help say "part of a refund"; a filer electing the whole refund may answer No, and line 78a is 0 with the refund paid to the filer. No other question or refusal covers Form IT-195. No tax amount is wrong; the election is lost. Low; BUG-0449.

unruled:ny_it201.ask.us_obligation_inter.reason: Line 28 screen: whether interest or dividends came from U.S. government obligations or a fund holding them; Yes refuses line 28, No computes $0.

findings.evidence: ny_it201i p. 9, Line 28 limits the fund subtraction to a regulated investment company that 'meet[s] the 50% asset requirement each quarter' and to 'the portion of the qualifying dividends ... derived from federal obligations'. A fund that fails the test, or qualifies only in part, answers Yes and the refusal only costs coverage.

unruled:ny_it201.ask.414h#1.reason: Line 21 screen: asks whether a Form W-2 from the public job shows a 414(h) contribution; Yes refuses line 21, No computes $0.

findings.evidence: The question (expr.source) asks whether you or, on a joint return, your spouse is a public employee in one of the listed systems 'with 414(h) retirement contributions shown on a Form W-2' - any W-2, not one particular job's; the label alone is short.

A box 14 amount labelled by a system's name rather than '414(h)' may not be recognized; the question names the systems and usually the box. A presentation residual, no amount wrong where the filer recognizes it.

unruled:ny_it201.ask.529_nonqualified#1.reason: Line 22 screen: whether a 2025 New York 529 withdrawal was for anything but college, career training or student loans; Yes refuses line 22 and its worksheet, No computes $0.

findings.evidence: The question defines nonqualified against 'qualified higher education expenses at an eligible college or other post-secondary institution'; a non-eligible school is a Yes.
The question says 'a qualified education loan of the beneficiary or the beneficiary's sibling'; that is the IRC 221(d) term the finding asks for.
The question lists 'a rollover to a Roth IRA' without the 529(c)(3)(E) conditions; a nonqualifying rollover could be answered No. Wording, no value where the rollover qualifies.

unruled:ny_it201.ask.529_owner#1.reason: Line 30 screen: whether the filer, as account owner, put money into or took money out of the New York 529 account; Yes refuses line 30, No computes $0.

findings.evidence: The question covers the beneficiary who is not the owner: 'or, as a beneficiary, receive a withdrawal included in federal adjusted gross income'.
The question says 'you (or, on a joint return, your spouse)'.
A qualified withdrawal included in no federal AGI asks the question and leaves line 30 zero; extra asking, no wrong value.

unruled:ny_it201.ask.abode_part_year#1.reason: Line 59 screen: whether a month of 2025 had a New York home for half the month or less; Yes refuses line 59, No uses the full sales and use tax chart.

findings.evidence: The example is a filer who arrived June 10: ny_it201i p. 3 says 'If you moved into New York State on any day other than January 1 ... see New York nonresidents and part-year residents', and line 1 refuses a part-year or nonresident filer (gate.part_year_state, forms/ny/2025/ny_it201.yaml:486, citing 'If you were a New York State resident for only part of the year, do not file Form IT-201').

A spouse who maintained a New York permanent place of abode for only part of 2025 is a part-year resident, and line 1 refuses a joint return with a spouse who was not a full-year New York State and City resident (gate.spouse_nonresident, forms/ny/2025/ny_it201.yaml:495; ny_it201i p. 3, 'If one of you was a New York State resident and the other was a nonresident or part-year resident, you must each file a separate New York return').

ny_it201i p. 18 prorates only where the filer 'maintained a permanent place of abode in New York State for sales and use tax purposes for only part of the year', and a two-week rental is not a permanent place of abode. A Yes from a filer who reads 'home' broadly only refuses line 59 (correct amount: the full chart), so no computed amount changes.

unruled:ny_it201.ask.city_credits#1.class: no defect; the other two credits are refused before the question
unruled:ny_it201.ask.city_credits#1.reason: Only the UBT credit can reach this question; the accumulation distribution and part-year credits are refused elsewhere.

findings.evidence: ny_it201i p. 15, Line 53 names three credits. The New York City accumulation distribution credit needs a trust distribution, reported on a Schedule K-1 (Form 1041), refused by scope.k1 (scope.schedule1), and is also on the IT-225 list (ny_it201.ask.it225: 'a trust's accumulation distribution'). The part-year resident City child care credit needs a part-year City resident, refused by ny_it201.gate.part_year_city. The question is asked only with a Schedule C (s1.has_sc), so the UBT credit is the one it must reach, and it names it.

unruled:ny_it201.ask.out_of_state_bond_i.reason: Line 20 screen: whether tax-free interest or dividends came from bonds issued outside New York or a fund holding them; Yes refuses line 20, No computes $0.

findings.evidence: The question names bonds and funds that invest in them; a fund of notes or other obligations is arguably outside it. Wording, no value where the fund holds bonds.
Accrued interest equal to the coupon leaves a zero addition; asking costs a question and changes no value.
The question says 'Did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) have interest or dividends from bonds of states other than New York...'.

unruled:ny_it201.ask.real_property_credi.reason: Line 67 screen: whether rent averaged $450 a month or less or real estate is worth $85,000 or less; Yes refuses line 67 (Form IT-214), No computes $0.

findings.evidence: IT-214-I p. 1 requires 'You occupied the same New York residence for six months or more' as a separate condition, which the screen does not ask. A filer who meets the rent or value test but not the six-month test answers Yes and only refuses line 67, whose correct amount is zero.

unruled:ny_it201.ask.special_accrual#1.reason: Lines 1 through 19 screen: whether income fixed in one year was reported federally in another after a move at the turn of the year; Yes refuses line 1, No takes federal line 1z.

findings.evidence: ny_it201i p. 31 limits a full-year resident's accrued income to 'non-New York source income that was fixed and determinable in a tax year prior to 2025, but you are reporting that income for federal income tax purposes in tax year 2025' (or income fixed in 2025 and reported later). New York source deferred pay needs no special accrual adjustment, so the over-broad Yes only refuses line 1 and never changes an amount.

unruled:gate:ny_it201.ask.city_resident#.class: no gate defect; a No to the City question refuses
unruled:gate:ny_it201.ask.city_resident#.reason: Every finding is a filer who answers the City question No, which refuses the New York return.

findings.evidence: A No to the City question always refuses: ny_it201.gate.part_year_city is ny_it201.ask.city_resident = false and refuses ny_it201.line1 (Form IT-360.1; 'This tool computes the New York City resident tax for a full-year City resident only'); ny_it201.state_resident_if_not_city only chooses which form the refusal names (gate.part_year_state, IT-203). So a wrong No is a refusal, never a silent amount (BUG-0748: both answers to the State question refuse). A full-year State resident outside the City is outside the tool (IT-201 for a non-City resident is not prepared).

ny_it201.ask.spouse_resident ('Did your husband or wife also live in New York City for all of 2025?') is asked on a joint return; a No refuses through ny_it201.gate.spouse_nonresident (ny_it201i p. 4, Item A).

The input's source asks residence 'by the same test with New York City in place of New York State'; the shown prompt 'Did you live in New York City ... for all of 2025?' is plainer. A statutory City resident domiciled elsewhere may answer No: A No to the City question always refuses: ny_it201.gate.part_year_city is ny_it201.ask.city_resident = false and refuses ny_it201.line1 (Form IT-360.1; 'This tool computes the New York City resident tax for a full-year City resident only'); ny_it201.state_resident_if_not_city only chooses which form the refusal names (gate.part_year_state, IT-203). So a wrong No is a refusal, never a silent amount (BUG-0748: both answers to the State question refuse).

A No to the City question always refuses: ny_it201.gate.part_year_city is ny_it201.ask.city_resident = false and refuses ny_it201.line1 (Form IT-360.1; 'This tool computes the New York City resident tax for a full-year City resident only'); ny_it201.state_resident_if_not_city only chooses which form the refusal names (gate.part_year_state, IT-203). So a wrong No is a refusal, never a silent amount (BUG-0748: both answers to the State question refuse). A domiciliary on a long assignment who answers No is refused, not mis-taxed.

unruled:gate:ny_it201.ask.est_any#1.reason: Yonkers is refused before line 75 matters.

findings.evidence: ny_it201.ask.yonkers asks whether you or your spouse lived, worked or had a place in Yonkers in 2025 and refuses (ny_it201.gate.yonkers, ny_it201i p. 5, Item D2). A filer whose only prepayment was to Yonkers has a Yonkers connection and never reaches line 75; ny_it201i p. 22 also lists 'New York State, New York City, Yonkers' payments in the question's amount help.

unruled:gate:ny_it201.ask.est_any#1.adjudication: round F sampled-review adjudication, 2026-11-21 (Claude agents, RUBRIC2)

unruled:gate:ny_it201.ask.owes_use_tax#1.reason: Both findings are answered by the abode question's help and by the fact that only full-year New York City residents reach the question.

findings.evidence: The help reads 'The chart amount is for a full year and is cut by months without a New York home' (interview/ny/2025/questions.yaml:254-256), so a month with no home is a month with a home for 'half the month or less'. A January 10-June 30 abode gives July-December months with no home; the filer answers Yes and is refused. The page counts only a part-month over half as a month (ny_it201i p. 18, 'Count any period you maintained the abode for more than one-half of a month as one month').

The tool is asked only of full-year New York City residents (ny_it201.gate.part_year_city), whose locality is New York City, so 'a lower rate than New York City's' is the p. 18 test: 'You owe use tax to the second locality if you were a resident of that locality at the time of the purchase, and its rate of tax is higher than the rate of tax originally paid.' The reviewer's example compares the other state's rate with an 8.0% county, which is not the locality of a city resident; if the other state's rate is not below the city's the filer answers No, and a mistaken Yes only costs coverage.

unruled:gate:ny_it201.ask.owes_use_tax#1.adjudication: round F sampled-review adjudication, 2026-11-21 (Claude agents, RUBRIC2)

unruled:gate:ny_it201.estimated_payments.reason: The line-75 gate only guards the 'late or short installment' question; the balance-due test guards the no-installment case.

findings.evidence: A filer with no estimates and too little withholding is caught by ny_it201.est_penalty_balance: a balance due (ny_it201.tax_due_positive) with prepayments below the safe harbor (ny_it201.est_below_safe_harbor) sets ny_it201.gate.estimated_penalty, which refuses line 81 (Form IT-2105.9). ny_it201i p. 23: 'You may owe a penalty: if line 80 is $300 or more and represents more than 10%...; or if you underpaid your estimated tax liability for any payment period.'

The cited sentence is the general statement; the encoding tests both p. 23 conditions in ny_it201.gate.estimated_penalty (balance path) and ny_it201.est_penalty_late (installment path). The line-75 gate is only a precondition of the installment question, since withholding is spread evenly by default; no amount changes.
A filer with positive estimates all paid on time answers No to ny_it201.ask.est_late and is not refused; the question only costs an extra screen.

unruled:gate:ny_it201.estimated_payments.adjudication: round F sampled-review adjudication, 2026-11-21 (Claude agents, RUBRIC2)

unruled:gate:ny_it201.has_edu_account#1.reason: The federal account question already covers beneficiaries and spouses, and a taxable beneficiary withdrawal is refused federally.

findings.evidence: person.x_edu_account asks 'did you have a 529 plan, a Coverdell education savings account or an ABLE account, or was one held for you?' and its help says 'A Form 1099-Q or Form 1099-QA sent to you for 2025 means Yes' (interview/2025/questions.yaml:3513-3519), so a beneficiary is counted; and a withdrawal included in federal AGI is a taxable distribution that person.x_edu_taxable ('A Yes ends the interview here') refuses through person.x_other.

The gate is broader than the cited owner test (any 529, Coverdell or ABLE account, held or owned), so it never excludes a New York 529 owner; the narrower cited condition is then asked by ny_it201.ask.ny_529. No amount changes.

A holder of an out-of-state 529, Coverdell or ABLE account is asked 'own an account in New York's 529 college savings program?', answers No (help: 'A 529 plan of another state... counts as No'), and lines 22 and 30 stay zero as ny_it201i p. 10 gives them no amount; extra asking only.

unruled:gate:ny_it201.has_edu_account#1.adjudication: round F sampled-review adjudication, 2026-11-21 (Claude agents, RUBRIC2)

unruled:gate:ny_it201.has_other_income#1.reason: Any federal inclusion of the check is on Schedule 1 line 1 or inside line 9, and the question's own wording names both.

findings.evidence: Schedule 1 Part I lines 8a-8z total to line 9, and a state payment included in federal income is either a taxable refund (line 1) or other income (line 9); the gate s1.line1 > 0 or s1.line9 <> 0 (ny_it201.has_other_income) tests both, and the question says 'as a state tax refund or as other income'. No other federal line plausibly carries it (ny_it201i p. 8, Line 25).
The gate is a prefilter on where an included inflation check can appear, not a restatement of the p. 8 event; the event itself is asked by ny_it201.ask.inflation_check. No amount changes.
A filer with other Schedule 1 income and no inflation check answers No, and line 25 refuses only on a Yes (ny_it201.gate.line25); extra asking only.

unruled:gate:ny_it201.has_other_income#1.adjudication: round F sampled-review adjudication, 2026-11-21 (Claude agents, RUBRIC2)

unruled:gate:ny_it201.has_tax_exempt#1.reason: The gate is a superset of the line 20 condition; both findings are extra asking.

findings.evidence: The gate (any federal tax-exempt interest or exempt-interest dividends) is wider than ny_it201i p. 7's 'states other than New York State', and the gated question narrows it: 'Did any of your tax-free interest or dividends come from bonds issued outside New York'. A New York-bond holder answers No; no amount changes.

A filer with only New York bond interest is asked once and answers No (help: 'Bonds of New York, its cities and agencies... are No'); line 20 stays $0 (ny_it201i p. 7, Line 20: out-of-state obligations only). Note, outside these findings: that gated prompt says 'your tax-free interest' without the spouse phrase although it is asked once per return (see the false-no ruling of this gate).

unruled:gate:ny_it201.has_tax_exempt#1.adjudication: round F sampled-review adjudication, 2026-11-21 (Claude agents, RUBRIC2)

unruled:gate:ny_it201.low_income#1.reason: The gate tests two necessary conditions of Form IT-214; it can only over-ask.

findings.evidence: ny_it214i p. 1 requires all of: 'Your federal adjusted gross income was $18,000 or less', six months in the same residence, full-year residency, and 'You could not be claimed as a dependent'. The gate keeps the first and last and the gated question's help states the six months; failing the gate means the credit is unavailable, and passing it only asks.
A part-year resident is refused earlier (ny_it201.gate.part_year_state / ny_it201.gate.part_year_city); ny_it214i p. 1 says 'You were a New York State resident for all of 2025'.

unruled:gate:ny_it201.low_income#1.adjudication: round F sampled-review adjudication, 2026-11-21 (Claude agents, RUBRIC2)

unruled:gate:ny_it201.moved#1.reason: Within the return this tool accepts (full-year New York City residents), the two move events are the whole of the p. 31 residency conditions.

findings.evidence: A filer who moved into New York State outside New York City is not a full-year New York City resident, so ny_it201.gate.part_year_city refuses (ask.city_resident = No); ny_it201i p. 31 'Full-year New York State residents' applies only to such a filer.
A New York City part-year resident ('New York City part-year resident for tax year 2025', ny_it201i p. 31) is refused by ny_it201.gate.part_year_city.

For a full-year New York City resident the p. 31 conditions are exactly 'nonresident of New York City on December 31, 2024... but... full-year New York City resident for 2025' (ny_it201.ask.moved_in) or 'will be a New York City nonresident on January 1, 2026' (ny_it201.ask.moved_out), and accrued income is asked in ny_it201.ask.special_accrual; no amount changes.
A filer who moved in on January 1, 2025 with no accrued income is asked ny_it201.ask.special_accrual and answers No; extra asking only.

unruled:gate:ny_it201.moved#1.adjudication: round F sampled-review adjudication, 2026-11-21 (Claude agents, RUBRIC2)

unruled:gate:ny_it201.ny_529_if_account#.reason: The owner gate names the spouse; the two gated follow-ups do not, which is where a joint spouse's activity is lost.

findings.evidence: A beneficiary's withdrawal 'included in your federal adjusted gross income' (ny_it201i p. 10) is a taxable 529 distribution, which the federal question person.x_edu_taxable ('A Yes ends the interview here', person.x_other) refuses before the New York part; and ny_it201.ask.ny_529 help says 'an account someone else owns for you, counts as No'.

The gate itself asks 'did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) own an account', so a spouse-only owner reaches the follow-ups; but those (interview/ny/2025/questions.yaml:145-156) say 'did you put money into that account, or take any out' and 'did you take money out' with a bare 'you', so the spouse's contribution or withdrawal on the joint return can be answered No and lost (ny_it201i p. 10: '$10,000 for married taxpayers filing a joint return').

ny_it201i p. 10 asks 'make contributions to or a withdrawal from'; the gate asks ownership (any time in 2025, including closed or moved accounts) and ny_it201.ask.529_owner then asks the contribution or withdrawal. An owner with no activity answers No there. No amount changes.
An owner with no 2025 contribution or withdrawal answers No to ny_it201.ask.529_owner and ny_it201.ask.529_nonqualified; lines 22 and 30 are zero as ny_it201i p. 10 ('If No, go to line 31') says.

unruled:gate:ny_it201.ny_529_if_account#.adjudication: round F sampled-review adjudication, 2026-11-21 (Claude agents, RUBRIC2)

unruled:gate:ny_it201.pension_59_known#1.class: no gate defect; the findings read the choice backwards
unruled:gate:ny_it201.pension_59_known#1.reason: When no recipient was born in 1965 or earlier the question is asked; when one was, line 29's refusal applies without it.

findings.evidence: ny_it201.pension_exclusion_if_young asks ny_it201.ask.pension_exclusion when pension_59_known is false: 'Did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) turn 59½ by December 31, 2025, or receive any of that pension or IRA money as the beneficiary of someone who died?'. A person born January to June 1966 answers Yes and is refused (ny_it201.pension_exclusion_line, gate.line29).
The same question names the beneficiary case and is asked whenever no recipient was born in 1965 or earlier.

The choice gives No only when a recipient was born in 1965 or earlier, and then ny_it201.pension_exclusion_line is true from pension_59_known itself; when the condition is false the question is asked. Both branches reach line 29.

ny_it201i p. 9, Line 29: "If you became 59½ during 2025, enter only the amount you received after you became 59½". Births in 1965 (59½ before or during 2025) can have a line 29 amount, so treating them as eligible (a refusal) is right; births to June 1966 are asked.

unruled:gate:ny_it201.public_job_if_w2#1.reason: The gate is a W-2 prefilter on the same population; both findings are presentation or extra asking.

findings.evidence: The question groups New York City and the counties; ny_it201i p. 15 says tax applies when earnings 'allocated to either zone exceed $50,000'. A filer with $40,000 in each zone answers Yes and is refused although MCTMT is $0: extra refusing, no wrong amount (rule 2).
'self-employment earnings' read as gross receipts can only exceed net earnings (ny_it201i p. 15-16, net earnings from self-employment), so the filer answers Yes more often, never No wrongly.

'came from business done in New York City or the nearby counties' read as unallocated total can only overstate the zone amount; a reading as the allocated share gives the right answer. Any wrong reading errs toward Yes.

unruled:ny_it201.ask.city_credits#2.reason: The question names UBT only because the other two credits are refused or unreachable; the one real gap is the missing spouse phrase.

findings.evidence: The accumulation distribution credit needs an accumulation distribution from a trust (ny_it201i, Form IT-201-ATT instructions, Line 9: 'If you received an accumulation distribution as a beneficiary of a trust'); the same distribution on federal Form 4970 is an IT-225 item (ny_it201i p. 7: 'do include on your Form IT-225, line 5 the amount of income you reported on Form 4970'), and ny_it201.ask.it225 names 'an accumulation distribution' and refuses line 23 (gate ny_it201.gate.it225).

'part-year resident nonrefundable New York City child and dependent care credit' (ny_it201i p. 15) is for a part-year NYC resident; ny_it201.gate.part_year_city refuses anyone not a full-year NYC resident (ny_it201.ask.city_resident = No).

The bank prompt (interview/ny/2025/questions.yaml:210) reads 'Did your business pay...' with no spouse phrase, though it is asked once per return and the gate counts either spouse's Schedule C; under interview/README.md a bare 'your' that leaves out the spouse's item on a joint return is a defect (the sibling ny_it201.ask.mctmt names the spouse). The partner/LLC-member part of the finding cannot be settled from the archived pages (they do not describe who may claim the UBT credit), and partners without a Schedule C never reach the question because the gate is s1.has_sc (gate reviewed separately).

A non-resident of the city is refused earlier by ny_it201.gate.part_year_city, and for a city resident who paid UBT the credit is what line 53 holds (ny_it201i p. 15, 'complete Section C of Form IT-201-ATT'); a Yes only costs coverage.

'for 2025' reads as UBT for tax year 2025, the year the credit and Form NYC-202 follow (ny_it201i p. 15); a payment made in 2025 for 2024 is not for 2025. The archived pages do not define the credit year, so any further doubt costs a refusal at most, not a value.
